# Unknowns and risks

The plan rests on one open call, [[11-unknowns-and-risks#UNK-051 Text call|who settles whether meeting text may leave the laptop]], and most of the other unknowns and risks wait on it. The security review pack, the impact assessment and the full data list each have an owner and an ask-by date but no author yet. Five more unknowns came from the desks session: who calls the lock, whether any design or trial exists, how Heron would read Zoom, whether a digest is a client record, and whether Client Delivery knows what Heron surfaces about them. The requirements session added three more, each holding up a requirement it wrote: how many organizers turn transcripts on, which decides how often a note is calendar-only; whether a digest held until first login is acceptable; and whether accepted invitees count as being in a meeting. It also added the risk that thin calendar-only notes pile up. The allocation session added one more, [[11-unknowns-and-risks#UNK-075 Acceptance in the calendar read|whether the calendar read carries each invitee's response]]. The newest is [[11-unknowns-and-risks#UNK-076 Council vote on the pilot|whether the works council votes on the pilot]]; if it does vote, that is a further gate on the pilot, on top of the unknowns that list the February pilot under what they block. The rows under Question ledger show how each owed question ended; most now wait on the text call, on [[11-unknowns-and-risks#UNK-071 Lawful basis for each source|the lawful basis for each source]] or on [[11-unknowns-and-risks#UNK-068 Who builds Consent and identity|who builds Consent and identity]].

## Unknowns

### UNK-051 Text call

Nobody has settled whether meeting text may leave the laptop in the pilot, and no paper says who has the authority to call it. The CISO allows nothing off the laptop and the product owner's design has a cloud service writing the summaries.

- **Question:** Who settles whether meeting, mail and document text may leave the laptop in the pilot, and which design is meant?
- **Owner:** @solution-lead (Solution lead)
- **State:** open
- **Ask by:** 2026-11-06
- **Opened:** 2026-10-12
- **Notes:** The solution lead believes the CIO settles it as budget holder, with no source named, so this is a belief and not a finding. The two ends are the CISO's rule and the product owner's cloud design. The CIO's brief also says the data never leaves the machine, which the product owner's one-pager contradicts; both are plans, not facts.

### UNK-052 CISO line reaching the CIO

- **Question:** Has the CISO's position reached the CIO, who settles the text call, and who tells them if not?
- **Owner:** @solution-lead (Solution lead)
- **Ask:** @cio
- **State:** open
- **Ask by:** 2026-11-06
- **Opened:** 2026-10-12

### UNK-058 Security review pack

The CISO wants the review pack by 10 November, and nobody is recorded as writing it. The pilot start of 2 February 2027 depends on whether the six-week app-registration review sits inside the booked review or runs after it.

- **Question:** Who writes the security review pack, and does the booked review (pack by 10 November, review the week of 16 November, outcome by 4 December) already include the six-week app-registration review, or does that review start after 4 December?
- **Owner:** @ciso (CISO)
- **State:** open
- **Blocks:** [[04b-releases#Release one: February pilot, Client Delivery London|February pilot]]; the ledger rows that wait on it are under Question ledger
- **Ask by:** 2026-11-06
- **Opened:** 2026-10-12
- **Notes:** If the booked review is the six-week review, the CISO's 4 December date is shorter than the "about six weeks" they quoted, and one of the two figures is wrong. If the six weeks starts after 4 December, it ends around 15 January 2027, after the January packaging and close to the 2 February pilot start. The solution lead's view is that this is what the CIO call needs to settle first, and that a registration review on top of the booking puts the February start in doubt. [[sources#SRC-009|The CISO's position]] and [[sources#SRC-010|the booking]] give the two figures. The solution lead says the CISO is the fallback for any doubt about the pack or the registration review.

- **Question:** Who writes the full list of data Heron reads, by what date so the works council has it before its December meeting, does it include the team adoption dashboard, and what must legal counsel's constraints leave out of it?

The solution lead also expects legal counsel to have constraints on what goes in, with no source yet. As far as the vault knows, the list covers calendar entries, mail, documents, Teams transcripts and the team adoption dashboard. The solution lead is not sure who writes the list and hands it to the product owner and the works council to settle; no one is recorded as writing it.

### UNK-067 How slow is too slow

Nobody has said how long the Summarizer may take before the Desktop agent gives up and shows nothing, so "slow" has no number.

Ask-by moved to 2026-10-29 by the solution lead, who says a later date misses the 10 November pack deadline. ## Risks

### R-01 Two ends, nobody picks

The CISO and the product owner are at opposite ends on whether text leaves the laptop, and if nobody makes them pick, the team reaches January still arguing, packaging does not happen and the February pilot slips.

- **Owner:** @solution-lead (Solution lead)
- **State:** open

### R-02 Digest fails the first morning

The first digest may name someone who was only mentioned or flag a deadline far in the future, and if a reader sees more than a couple of those she stops reading within the week.

- **Owner:** @solution-lead (Solution lead)
- **State:** open

### R-03 No boundary with the desk agent team

The desk agent team may be handed Heron with no line between what they own and what the product owner owns, and then spend February designing and ship nothing by April.

- **Owner:** @solution-lead (Solution lead)
- **State:** open

### R-04 Thin notes pile up

If few organizers turn transcripts on, most notes are written from the calendar entry alone, and a reader whose team stops reading after three wrong items may stop reading the thin ones too. The solution lead wants the product owner to see this.

- **Owner:** @product-owner (Product owner)
- **State:** open
- **Notes:** Raised by the solution lead in the requirements session, who names Sam's team as the one that stops reading after three wrong items and says Sam is @pilot-lead; the product owner has not been asked. How common calendar-only notes are waits on [[11-unknowns-and-risks#UNK-072 How many organizers turn transcripts on|the count of organizers who turn transcripts on]]. The solution lead adds that if people refuse transcript reading when consent is asked per source, calendar-only notes become more common and the feature may die at the three-wrong-items tolerance; nobody has a figure for how many would refuse.
